question: Portuguese organisation Gerador has had three applications to the Creative Europe programme rejected for supposedly breaching a rule imposing a three-application limit per organisation. Gerador consented and took part in only three proposals, however.

It was excluded because its participant identification code (PIC) was wrongly used in a fourth application submitted by third parties that did not have Gerador’s permission or signature. The Executive Agency (EACEA) has confirmed that the system allows other parties’ PICs to be included even if they do not confirm their involvement at the submission stage.
This security flaw means reputable organisations can be ‘blocked’ or penalised for abusive actions by others. 1.
Is the Commission aware of this structural flaw in the portal, which allows organisations to be added to applications without their express consent and without a verification mechanism at the EACEA?
What urgent measures does the Commission intend to take to fix the system and make sure an organisation’s PIC can only be used in an application if the organisation confirms electronically?

Will the Commission instruct EACEA to immediately reassess the admissibility of their legitimate projects by organisations like Gerador, which have not given their permission to be included in more than the maximum number of projects?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The Funding and Tenders Portal1 is the main entry point for funding programmes and procurement procedures managed by the Commission and other EU institutions and agencies, enhancing transparency and accessibility.

Under the CREA-CULT-2025-COOP call, the European Education and Culture Executive Agency (EACEA) has received complaints concerning alleged ‘inclusions without consent’. Any intentional inclusion without consent constitutes misrepresentation under the EU Financial Regulation and may lead to rejection and/or administrative sanctions.

Responsibility for the accuracy of the information submitted, including consent to participate, lies with the coordinators. These complaints are under investigation by EACEA. The Commission acknowledges the importance of strengthening safeguards while not increasing administrative burden.

For the CREA-CULT-2026-COOP call, the maximum of three applications per organisation will apply only to coordinators or partners, which can check their inclusion in applications, and will not include associated partners or affiliated entities. Coordinators must obtain from each participating organisation a written declaration confirming its consent to participate.

These measures will contribute to preventing similar situations. Several organisations have submitted requests for redress, which are being examined in accordance with applicable procedures. EACEA is investigating the complaints and will reply in due course. Where justified, proposals may be re-evaluated.
Any follow-up will be determined on a case-by-case basis, ensuring equal treatment and full respect of the applicable legal framework.
